osmTags.inscription: This unusual house was used from the late 18th centery as a Chapel by A Presbyterian sect called the Auld licht. The Large windows on the riverside were to light the meeting room. Part of the building was removed in the 1950s to widen Millrow.
In 1842 Her Majesty's Commissioners gave a lease of this grass yard of Dunblane as a bleaching Green for the inhabitants.
Dunblane takes its name from 'the hill fort of Blane'. A Celtic Saint. There is a strong local tradition that the town was first established on Holmehill early in the 7th Century.

eras.summary: Location and terrain only. OpenStreetMap has no mapped outline for this site.
eras.basis: Everything drawn is traced from OpenStreetMap ways (ODbL) and the Terrarium elevation tiles. Each element names its OSM way.
eras.conjecture: Walls and buildings without a sourced height are drawn as kerb-high plan lines, never as masses. Closed walls have no gates: none are mapped. The DEM is ~30 m source resolution: it cannot show terraces, ditches or scarps. Nothing historic is depicted.
